newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian truckers threaten new national strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian truckers threaten new national strike.

text.p: Colombia's main truck drivers' organization declared an "amber alert" Tuesday and threatened to launch a new nationwide strike, a truckers' representative said.

Luz Marie Tongarife, executive director of Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC), said drivers in the Caribbean port city of Cartagena ceased operations Monday to protest freight owners' failure to fulfill the terms of an agreement that ended a five day stoppage at the end of last month.
She said the rest of the association, which represents about 85 percent of truckers' across the country, could declare a solidarity strike later in the day.
ACC chairman Javier Suarez is in Cartagena to meet local truckers' representatives and freight owners in a bid to mediate the new dispute.

"We're just waiting for word from our chairman. This dispute could generalize in the rest of the country if things get worse in Cartagena and truckers would support the strike across the rest of Colombia," Tongarife told Reuters.

The last national truckers' strike, which lasted from April 20 through 25, paralyzed transport operations across much of the country and delayed the shipment of at least 200,000 60-kg bags of coffee, according National Coffee Growers' Federation officials.
Tongarife said freight owners were still not fulfilling the terms of the deal they signed to end the first truckers' strike, an 11-day stoppage, last October.
Terms of the accord included a 30 percent hike in freight rates, payments for waiting time and a revision of vehicle licensing taxes and regulations regarding the age of vehicles.
Tongarife said no ACC truckers were transporting cargoes -- mainly imported barley, containers and metal sheeting -- out of the port of Cartagena.

Cartagena handles about 30 percent of Colombia's key coffee exports, with most of the remainder shipped out through the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura. It was not immediately clear what effect the Cartagena stoppage was having on the transport of coffee into the port.
